summary:
Brandenburg stands under the national framework of Germany: the constitutional, equality and identity-document regime of the Federal Republic applies in the Land, and no Land-level instrument displaces it. The region-specific material available here consists of two incidents in Cottbus concerning public LGBT life.

Lausitzer Rundschau reported a fire at the Regenbogenkombinat, an LGBT venue in Cottbus, shortly before the city's CSD, which prompted an investigation by the Staatsschutz. Neither the circumstances of the fire nor the outcome of that investigation are sourced, and no finding of an anti-LGBT motive has been reported.

Niederlausitz aktuell reported on 26 October 2025 that the CSD parade in Cottbus went ahead under a large police deployment with two counter-demonstrations present. Organised counter-demonstrations at the city's principal LGBT public event are the only documented hostility signal in the Land for that period; no arrest figures, injury reports or trans-specific incidents connected with the parade are sourced.

Neither report concerns Land legislation or Land-level policy on gender recognition, custody, health care or sex-separated facilities. On those subjects the German national framework governs in Brandenburg as elsewhere in the country, and the national assessment should be consulted.
tangentialFactors:
Both Cottbus reports concern public LGBT organising rather than the legal position of an individual trans visitor, so they bear on the safety and visibility of public gatherings in the Land rather than on legal exposure.

The referral of the venue fire to the Staatsschutz indicates that Brandenburg authorities treat attacks on LGBT premises as politically motivated offences. Whether that produced a suspect, a charge or a motive finding is not recorded.

The 26 October 2025 parade took place with a large police deployment and two counter-demonstrations. No comparison with events in other German states appears in the sources, and there are no attendance or incident figures against which the event's risk level could be measured.
localsOnly:
Users of the Regenbogenkombinat in Cottbus have no sourced statement on whether the venue reopened after the fire or on any prosecution arising from it.

Participants in the Cottbus CSD on 26 October 2025 faced two counter-demonstrations alongside a large police presence; no arrests, injuries or follow-up measures affecting participants are reported.

No Brandenburg Land measure altering the legal position of trans residents in the Land beyond the national framework appears in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
The outcome of the Staatsschutz investigation into the Cottbus venue fire is unresolved; no motive finding, suspect or charge is sourced.

No Brandenburg Land statute, Land court decision or Land administrative practice on gender recognition, prison placement, health care or single-sex facilities is sourced here. How those matters are handled in the Land remains unverified.

The two Cottbus items are raw counts: one fire at an LGBT venue and one parade met by two counter-demonstrations. With no per-capita or statewide baseline, they establish no rate and support no ranking of the Land against others.
